# 06 Close the board: example, demo, glossary

## Outcome

An author can see sequence animation working without reading a test: `examples/sequence-full.srn`
carries a timeline exercising all four target kinds, `demos/sequence-diagram.html` steps through
it, and `CONTEXT.md` says what a sequence timeline can name.

## Why this ticket exists

The class-diagram board closed the same way, and the demo page currently states the opposite of
what is now true: "`SirenRenderResult.controller` is always `null` for a sequence diagram"
(`demos/sequence-diagram.html:27`, and again around `:60`). Documentation that contradicts the code
is worse than none.

`CONTEXT.md`'s **Timeline target** entry lists flowchart and class-diagram targets only, and its
**Lifeline** entry's `_Avoid_` line says "timeline (that is the animation block — a lifeline is
structural, not animated)", which is now half wrong: a lifeline is still structural, but it does
animate, with its participant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `examples/sequence-full.srn` gains a `timeline:` block at the end, naming at least one
      participant, one message, one control-flow block and one box grouping, and using at least
      one of each verb. It must produce **zero diagnostics** — including ticket 05's
      message-outlives-its-participant warning.
- [~] **No test renders every file in `examples/`.** The repo's established pattern is one inline
      source constant per example in `index.test.ts`, and the new sequence timeline test asserts
      zero diagnostics against that constant. Corrected after the final review: six of eight
      examples are covered this way, `complex-showcase.srn` and `step-reveal.srn` by nothing
      (pre-existing). The inline constant is byte-identical to the `.srn` today but **nothing
      enforces it** — a drift guard needs `@types/node`, which this package does not have
      (`lib` is ES2022+DOM, no `@types/node` installed). Left as a follow-up rather than adding a
      dependency unasked.
- [x] `demos/sequence-diagram.html` wires Next/Reset buttons to the returned controller for the
      full example, mirroring `demos/class-diagram.html:133-236`, and its prose no longer claims
      sequence diagrams have no controller.
- [x] `CONTEXT.md`'s **Timeline target** entry names a sequence diagram's four targets and states
      that a destroy mark animates with its participant.
- [x] `CONTEXT.md`'s **Lifeline** entry's `_Avoid_` line is corrected: a lifeline is structural and
      animates with its participant; "timeline" remains the wrong word for it.
- [x] **Sharpened by the round-1 review.** `CONTEXT.md`'s **Control-flow block** and **Box
      grouping** entries state their generated id convention (`loop:1`, `alt:2`, `box:1`), matching
      how the **Namespace** and **Note** entries already document `namespace:1` / `note:1`. The
      repo's own precedent is that a generated id an author types is glossary material; ticket 02
      minted these and the glossary has not caught up.
- [x] `CONTEXT.md`'s **Message** entry is checked against ticket 02's change — its `${from}-${to}`
      id convention is deliberately unchanged, so it should need no edit. Confirm rather than
      assume.
- [x] **Found by ticket 07, outside its write scope.**
      `packages/core/src/theme/default.css` (the comment above `.siren-pending`, ~line 470) still
      says "renderToSVG.ts only marks elements that actually have an `enter` action".
      `renderToSVG.ts` now marks nothing — ticket 07 deleted both `pendingElementIds` copies and
      moved step 0 to `establishStepZero()` in `render()`. The CSS rule itself is correct and all
      theme tests pass; this is comment rot only. Point it at `createAnimationController`'s
      `computeClassStateAtStep`.
- [x] `.dev/mermaid-diagram-roadmap.md` marks board 2 done and names board 3 (author styling) as
      next.
